reason: Under the arithmetic lens the claimed gains do not hold. (1) Metric units in the exp39 lab: D = TP+FP+FN = 122151+6846+6732 = 135729, so one FN->TP is worth +7.4e-6 J, one FP removed +6.6e-6, and GT edges/D = 0.95. N_pred is fixed by construction, so the node-multiplier term is exactly 0. One extra division TP is worth 0.1/194 = +0.0005. (2) The +0.048 swap/u_diverted/v_taken oracle is out of reach: those matches sit 3.9-4.5 um from GT, while xy grid error is at most 0.81 um per axis (RMS 0.47). De-quantisation can only flip matches whose Hungarian margin is under ~1 um, which is a small tail (<~3%) of those classes. (3) Direct dose-response, measured on 24 videos: adding one more xy quantisation (+0.22 um^2/axis) cost edge recall -0.0021 on 44b6 and -0.0013 on 6bba, before linefit. The loss is convex, so perfectly removing the existing quantisation gains at most that much. Allowing that each flipped match can also turn our edge into an FP (x1-2) and scaling by 0.95 gives a pre-linefit ceiling of +0.0012..+0.004 J. (4) Linefit (the +0.0145 stage, i.i.d. variance factor ~0.23) already absorbs most i.i.d. grid noise before final matching; only relink and gap closing see raw coordinates. That leaves a standalone ceiling of about +0.0003..+0.002 for PERFECT de-quantisation. (5) Realistic capture is 50-80%: strided U-Nets are not shift-equivariant, the phase-consistency guard skips peaks, and 4 phases leave 0.014 um^2 residual. So standalone is about +0.0002..+0.0016. (6) The proportional read of x138 (-10% error = +0.007) does not apply. That gain includes learned BIAS correction (the 6bba mean z offset of 0.90 um is 0.81 um^2 of error, more than the whole xy grid variance of 0.44 um^2), float z output and trilinear edge-scorer features. Polyphase with per-video recentring removes xy grid variance only. (7) On top of the V1284 head, which removes largely the same grid error (the de-quantisation arithmetic predicts -11.7% against the head's -10.4%), the independent residual is <= +0.0005. The hypothesis claims +0.001..+0.004 on top of the head and +0.003..+0.006 standalone; both exceed the ceiling. Even the refined claim (+0.000..+0.001) cannot pass the +0.002 confirmation gate, and it contributes <5% of the +0.022 needed to reach 0.97.
fix_if_any: Only a bias-aware variant could exceed the gate arithmetically. Drop the per-video recentring for z and use the phase maps (or a z-sweep of the same trick) to estimate the systematic per-embryo offset (6bba z +0.9 um, y +0.3 um floor bias). Ship it only with float output coordinates, since z refinement dies at the int(round()) writer. That targets ~0.8-1.0 um^2 of bias rather than 0.44 um^2 of quantisation. But label-free bias estimation is exactly what lost 0.0031 on the LB (constant offset) and is largely what the learned head already does. Practical repair: fold it into the V1284 port as a cheap Phase-1 readout (24 videos, ~15 GPU-min, no scorer). Proceed only if GT-to-match distance drops >= 5% on both embryos ON TOP of the head's coordinates. Otherwise close it and spend the GPU hours on detection or duplicate-node work (the 1,907 no-node FN and the 606 short-track FN are larger pools).
realistic_public_gain: +0.000..+0.0005 on top of the V1284 head (the expected case); +0.0002..+0.0016 standalone if the head port stalls; the +0.048 oracle and the x138-proportional +0.003..+0.010 are not reachable. Below the +0.002 gate in expectation.
